questions.q: Salts of $A$ (atomic weight $8$), $B$ (atomic weight $18$) and $C$ (atomic weight $50$) were electrolysed under identical conditions using the same quantity of electricity. questions.solution:
According to the Faraday's law of electrolysis,

$W = ZQ = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q$

For the compound $A$,

Equivalent mass of $A$ = $\dfrac{Atomicmass}{Valency} = \dfrac{8}{x}$

$x$ is the valency factor for compound $A$.

So, $W = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q = \dfrac{\dfrac{8}{x}}{96500}Qx = \dfrac{7}{2 . 4 \times 96500}Q$

For compound $B$,

Equivalent mass of $B$=$\dfrac{Atomicmass}{Valency} = \dfrac{18}{y}$

$y$ is the valency factor for compound $B$.

So, $W = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q = \dfrac{\dfrac{18}{y}}{96500}Qy = \dfrac{27}{1 . 8 \times 96500}Q$

For compound $C$,

Equivalent mass of $C$ = $\dfrac{Atomicmass}{Valency} = \dfrac{50}{z}$

$z$ is the valency factor for compound $C$.

So, $W = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q = \dfrac{\dfrac{50}{z}}{96500}Qz = \dfrac{50}{7 . 5 \times 96500}Q$

Hence, $x: y: z = \dfrac{8}{2 . 4}: \dfrac{18}{1 . 8}: \dfrac{50}{7 . 5} = 3 . 33: 10: 6 . 66x: y: z = 1: 3: 2$

Hence, the valencies of $A, B$ and $C$ respectively are $1, 3, 2$.

The standard reduction potentials of $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\left|\mathrm{Zn}, \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\right| \mathrm{Cu}$ and $\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \mid \mathrm{Cu}$ and $\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \mid \mathrm{Ag}$ are respectively $-0.76,0.34$ and $0.8 \mathrm{ V}$. The following cells were constructed :
(1) $\mathrm{Zn}\left|\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\right|\left|\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\right| \mathrm{Cu}$
(2) $\mathrm{Zn}\left|\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}\right|\left|\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right| \mathrm{Ag}$
(3) $\mathrm{Cu}\left|\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \| \mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right| \mathrm{Ag}$
What is the correct order of $E_{\text{cell }}^{{}^{\circ}}$ of these cells?
questions.solution:
Given
$\mathrm{Zn}^{2+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn} \quad E^{{}^{\circ}}=-0.78 \mathrm{ V}\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu} \quad E^{{}^{\circ}}=0.34 \mathrm{ V}\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ag} \quad E^{{}^{\circ}}=0.8 \mathrm{ V}$
Cell reaction of (1) is
$\mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}+\mathrm{Cu}E_{\text{cell }}^{{}^{\circ}}=E_{\text{oxidation }}+E_{\text{reduction }}=+0.78+0.34=+1.12 \mathrm{ V}$
Cell reaction of (2) is
$\mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}+\mathrm{Ag}E_{\text{cell }}^{{}^{\circ}}=0.78+0.8=+1.58 \mathrm{ V}$
Cell reaction of (3) is :
$\mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{Ag}^{+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+\mathrm{Ag}E_{\text{cell }}^{{}^{\circ}}=-0.34+0.8=+0.46$
So, the correct order of $E_{\text{cell }}^{{}^{\circ}}$ of these cell is -
$\mathrm{b} > \mathrm{a} > \mathrm{c}.$
